listening1.context: You are going to hear a conversation between Maryam and Yousef.

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: Hi Yousef! Did you hear the announcement? Our school wants to cut its electricity bill, and the headmaster asked the science club for ideas.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Yes, I did. I think we should start by checking where the school wastes electricity. Shall we make a list?

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: Good idea. I noticed that the lights stay on in the empty classrooms during the break. That's a big waste.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: True. We can put a sign on each door that says, switch off the lights. Or we can ask the technician to fit sensors that turn off the lights automatically.

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: Sensors are expensive. Let's start with signs, and the students in each class can take turns to switch the lights off.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Okay. What about the air conditioners? They use the most electricity of all.

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: Yes. The classrooms are set at eighteen degrees, which is too cold. Twenty-four degrees is enough for everybody.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: I agree. The computers in the lab are also left on all night. We should turn them off before we go home.

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: Right. The lab teacher can check them every day at the end of the school day.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Now, what about the roof? The school has a big flat roof, and it gets a lot of sun.

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: You mean solar panels? Excellent idea, but the headmaster said they are too expensive this year. Maybe next year.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Then let's put that in the plan for next year. How long should our campaign last?

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: One month is enough to see a change. After that, we can read the meter and compare the results.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Great. Who shall we invite to launch the campaign? The headmaster?

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: I think the Director of Education would be better. It will make the students take it more seriously.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Good point. Finally, what shall we call our campaign?

script.speaker: Maryam
script.text: How about Switch Off, Save On? It's short and easy to remember.

items.q: Who asked the science club for ideas?
What will the students put on each classroom door?
What temperature will they set the air conditioners to?
Who will check the computers every day?
What will the school do next year?
How long will the campaign last?
What will the campaign be called?

listening2.context: You are going to hear a talk about recycling paper and glass.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Today I am going to talk about recycling paper and glass, two easy ways to protect our environment.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Let us start with paper. Paper is made from wood, so making new paper means cutting down trees. When we recycle one tonne of paper, we save about seventeen trees. Recycling paper also uses less water and less energy than making new paper.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: How is paper recycled? First, the used paper is collected and taken to a factory. Then it is mixed with water to make a soft mixture. After that, workers clean it and press it into new sheets. However, paper cannot be recycled for ever. The fibres become shorter each time, so paper can be recycled only five to seven times.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Now let us talk about glass. Glass is made from sand, and it can be recycled again and again without losing its quality. A bottle that you put in the recycling bin today can become a new bottle in a few weeks.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Recycling glass saves a lot of energy, because broken glass melts at a lower temperature than sand. This is important because a glass bottle that is thrown away can stay in the ground for thousands of years.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Before glass is recycled, it is sorted by colour into clear, green and brown glass. Window glass and mirrors must not be mixed with bottles, because they melt in a different way.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: What can you do? Use the special bins that many towns now have near shops and schools. Wash the bottles and jars first, and keep the paper dry and clean. Small actions by many people make a big difference.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Thank you for listening.

short.q: How many trees do we save when we recycle one tonne of paper?
How many times can paper be recycled?
Into which three colours is glass sorted?

tf.statement: Glass loses its quality every time it is recycled.
Window glass can be mixed with bottles.
